thesis: Broadcom is a $30+ billion quarterly revenue technology company dominating hidden infrastructure via semiconductor solutions (AI accelerators and networking) and enterprise software, revealing why most consumers know the brand minimally despite its massive scale.

facts.claim: Q3 2026 consolidated revenue reached $29.6 billion, up 86% year-over-year, with semiconductors representing 70% and infrastructure software 30% of revenue.
AI semiconductor revenue grew 221% year-over-year to $16.7 billion in Q3 2026, driven by custom AI accelerators and networking chips that power data centers globally.
Infrastructure software segment operating margin reached 84% in Q3 2026 with 94% gross margin, making it the highest-margin business despite being 30% of revenue.
Broadcom's current form is built through major acquisitions including legacy Broadcom, Avago Technologies, VMware, Brocade, CA Technologies, and Symantec.
The company generated $10.3 billion in free cash flow in Q2 2026 from $10.5 billion operating cash, reflecting powerful cash conversion despite capital intensity.
Broadcom semiconductor solutions serve enterprise data centers, AI systems, networking equipment, storage systems, broadband access, telecom, wireless devices and industrial automation.

verified_numbers.context: Expected Q4 2026 AI semiconductor revenue, up 236% year-over-year

timeline.event: Broadcom acquired VMware for enterprise software segment expansion
Q2 revenue hit record $22.2 billion with AI semiconductor revenue $10.8 billion, up 143% year-over-year
